messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Area | Key Statutes / Regulations | Practical Take‑aways | |------|---------------------------|-----------------------| | **Seat Belt & Child Restraint** | *Tex. Transportation Code § 545.001* – All drivers and front‑seat passengers must wear seat belts; rear‑seat occupants under 8 years old must use approved child restraints. | • Install a proper child seat before the vehicle’s first trip.
• Failure to buckle up can result in a $50 fine plus points on your license. | | **Speed Limits** | *Tex. Transportation Code § 545.021* – Speed limits vary by road type; posted limits are mandatory unless otherwise indicated. | • Pay attention to “no speed limit” zones (e.g., some rural highways).
• Exceeding limits by 20 mph or more can lead to higher fines and possible license suspension. | | **DUI / Alcohol** | *Tex. Transportation Code §§ 545.041–545.045* – Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal for most drivers; lower thresholds apply to commercial drivers and those under 21. | • A BAC of 0.05% or higher can still trigger a DUI charge for commercial drivers.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and mandatory alcohol education programs. | | **Texting & Phone Use** | *Tex. Transportation Code § 545.051* – Drivers may not hold a phone while operating a vehicle; hands‑free devices are allowed. | • Using a phone while driving can result in a $100 fine and points on your license. | | **Right‑of‑Way & Intersection Rules** | *Tex. Transportation Code §§ 545.031–545.036* – Standard right‑of‑way rules apply; special rules for school buses, emergency vehicles, and pedestrians. | • Yield to school buses when stopping to pick up or drop off children.
• Stop for emergency vehicles with flashing lights. | | **Parking & Loading Zones** | *Tex. Transportation Code § 545.061* – Parking restrictions vary by municipality; loading zones require a permit. | • Violations can lead to towing and a $25 fine. | | **Commercial Vehicle Regulations** | *Tex. Transportation Code §§ 545.040–545.046* – Additional requirements for commercial drivers, including stricter BAC limits and hours‑of‑service rules. | • Commercial drivers face harsher penalties for violations. | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | *Tex. Transportation Code § 545.001* – Annual registration renewal required; safety inspections mandated in some counties. | • Keep registration stickers current to avoid fines. | ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – Official source for traffic regulations, driver licensing, and enforcement updates. 2. **Texas Transportation Code** – Available online through the Texas Legislature’s website; review sections relevant to your situation. 3. **Local County Ordinances** – Some municipalities have additional rules (e.g., parking restrictions, speed limits). Check city or county websites. ### Quick Resources - **DPS Traffic Law Handbook** – PDF guide covering all major traffic laws. - **Texas Highway Patrol** – Enforcement agency; provides tips for safe driving. - **Legal Aid & Advocacy Groups** – For assistance if you’re facing a traffic violation or DUI charge. --- **Note:** Laws can change, so it’s wise to verify the latest statutes or consult legal counsel if you’re dealing with a specific case. If you’d like to see recent lawsuits involving traffic law violations in Texas, let me know and I can pull up relevant cases.
